reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that the wisdom of crowds does not necessarily imply superior performance unless the crowd is unbiased. The paper introduces a framework where the collective error γ is defined as the difference between realized value G and the crowd mean ⟨g⟩. This error can be decomposed into individual error ε and diversity δ through Page’s identity γ² = ε − δ. However, this identity is mathematically tautological and lacks predictive power. The key innovation lies in testing whether the crowd is unbiased using a p-value derived from a Gaussian null hypothesis. If the crowd mean ⟨g⟩ significantly deviates from G, then p < 0.05, indicating bias. In such cases, the ensemble may not outperform individual members, which is why the paper recommends a standing comparison between the best single model and the ensemble. The empirical result shows that even in biased crowds, the ensemble beats most members only ~67% of the time, suggesting that ensemble methods should be used conditionally rather than universally.
